thread:
pagerduty-bot: P1 - Elevated 5xx + timeouts on control-plane deps detected (alert group: controlplane-deps-5xx). Affected services: auth-service, org-lookup, config-api. Spike started at 2026-03-15T17:02:39Z. PagerDuty: paging SRE-Oncall.

Maria Gomez: Seeing global increase in 502/504 from gateway to auth & org-lookup. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/controlplane/errors (spike -> ~12% 5xx on prod). Anyone already on this?

SRE-Oncall: I'm on it. Paging in comms bridge -> starting live triage. Initial look: org-lookup latency is up, auth token endpoint timing out talking to billing-service.

Raj Patel: I rolled up logs from the gateways. Error pattern: upstream reset with "414 Request-URI Too Large" and a bunch of truncated headers before 502. Also some 504s from auth-service when calling billing.

Jamie Liu: Confirmed. Recent config rollout 2026-03-15 16:50UTC changed proxy header limits and also enabled extra user-metadata cookie. Could be related.

Maria Gomez: Good catch. If header size/cookie bloat + proxy header limit mismatch, gateway will return 502 and services downstream may time out retrying. Let's validate: can we reproduce on prod-staging?

Raj Patel: Quick repro against prod canary: curl -v -H "Cookie: large=..." https://api.redwood.internal/v1/org/lookup returns 502 with "upstream sent too big header".

Jamie Liu: Putting command here for oncall to test:

```
curl -i -H "Cookie: user_meta=$(head -c 5000 /dev/urandom | base64)" \
  "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/org/lookup?id=org_123"
```

Elaine Park: Customer impact: front-end error rate up for users that have large metadata cookies (SSO customers + partners using old cookie format). We have ~18 external customers with higher error rates, a few showing 50% session fails. Not wide but high severity for impacted customers.

SRE-Oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Roll back proxy header limit change (fast). 2) Apply a temporary rewrite to strip oversized cookies at the edge for specific paths. 3) Route traffic for heavy-cookie customers to fallback auth endpoint that ignores cookies. Which is fastest?

Maria Gomez: Rollback proxy change is the fastest. Deploy bot, can we rollback config-frontend:2026-03-15-1650?

deploy-bot: Initiating rollback of config-frontend to v2026-03-15-1645. CI checks pass. Starting canary rollback (10% -> 50% -> 100%). See: https://deploys.redwood.internal/rollbacks/3852

Raj Patel: While rollback runs, let's put a targeted rate limit and increase upstream timeout on auth-service to avoid cascade. Patch to auth svc envoy: set `upstream_read_timeout` to 8s (was 3s) for /v1/auth/token.

Jamie Liu: Pushing patch to staging then prod patch: `kubectl apply -f envoy-auth-timeout-patch.yaml` (will push as hotfix if rollback doesn't reach 100%).

Maria Gomez: Also start a small filter to drop large cookies on gateway for org/lookup path as a safety net. If rollback completes, we can remove filter.

SRE-Oncall: Confirmed rollback completed to 50% at +3m, 100% at +8m. Error rate on the dashboard dropped from 12% to 2% within 5 minutes of 100% rollback.

Elaine Park: Noting customer comms: affected customers list attached, reach out with "interruption" notice and root cause will be provided. Prioritize top 5 SLA customers for direct outreach.

Raj Patel: Post-mortem short notes: root cause = recent proxy header limits + new large cookie rollout exposed by SSO partner. Secondary issue = auth->billing calls timing out during retry storms, amplifying 5xx.

Jamie Liu: Action items (short-term):
- Revert proxy header config (done).
- Apply temporary cookie-strip filter for org/lookup (in PR: #4123).
- Increase upstream timeout for token endpoint (PR: #4125).

Maria Gomez: Action items (long-term):
- Add guardrail in CI to detect large header changes for proxies.
- Add traffic tag to identify heavy-cookie customers and route them to tolerant path.
- Update runbook: controlplane-deps -> include cookie-size checks and proxy header limits.

SRE-Oncall: Handoff: I will stay on for next 30m to confirm stability, then handoff to morning oncall (Jamie) at 00:00 UTC. Please update incidents@ with customer impact summary.

Elaine Park: I'll draft customer-facing note and coordinate with account teams. ETA 45m.

Maria Gomez: Quick timeline for the record:
- 17:02 UTC: Pager triggered.
- 17:06 UTC: Initial triage -> suspected header/cookie issue.
- 17:09 UTC: Rollback started.
- 17:17 UTC: Rollback completed 100%.
- 17:22 UTC: Error rates fell to baseline.

SRE-Oncall: Closing live mitigation phase — monitoring for 1 hour. If stable, we'll move to detailed postmortem.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback finished successfully. No deploy failures reported.

Maria Gomez: Thanks everyone. Tagging @jamie to own the postmortem writeup and runbook updates. @elaine follow up on customer comms. :thumbsup:

Jamie Liu: Acknowledged — will open postmortem draft and link it here when started.

pagerduty-bot: Incident P1 closed for alert group controlplane-deps-5xx (escalation suppressed).

SRE-Oncall: Final note for handoff: affected endpoints and customer list saved to incident ticket INC-2026-0412. If any recurrence, escalate immediately with the "header-limit" tag.

Elaine Park: Draft customer note posted to INC-2026-0412/comments. Leaving this channel for now, will pop back in when PMs reply.

Maria Gomez: Thanks all, closing thread.
